column2: Explainer: "A 90° Pd(II) corner plus a linear diamine linker gives a [Pd₂L₄]⁴⁺ cage"
column5: Fujita, Yazaki, Ogura JACS 1990, 112, 5645: (en)Pd(NO3)2 + 4,4'-bpy gives [(en)Pd(4,4'-bpy)]4(NO3)8 square (https://www.ims.ac.jp/en/about/publication/ann_rev_1997/vii-i-1.html); Pd2L4 cages from bare Pd(II) + banana-shaped bis-pyridyl ligands (Han, Engelhard, Clever, Chem Soc Rev 2014, https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2014/cs/c3cs60473j)

column2: q:1 explanation: "metal-nitrogen units replace some of the ether oxygens"
column5: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallacrown : ring of metal ions and heteroatoms with an [M-N-O] repeat unit; 12-crown-4 (8 C + 4 O) maps to 12-MC-4 (4 M + 4 N + 4 O), so M and N take the carbon positions; Pecoraro group page https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/pecoraro-lab/research/metallacrown-project/
column6: -> "metal ions and nitrogen atoms replace the ring carbons, giving a repeating M–N–O unit whose oxygens line the cavity"

column2: q:3 answer: "Switching to octahedral Fe(II) with the same ligands produces ... M₈L₆ cubes or M₄L₆ tetrahedra"
column5: Fe(II)4L6 tetrahedra use C2-symmetric bis-bidentate pyridylimine edge ligands (Hristova et al. 2011, Nitschke group; https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2011/sc/c0sc00495b); Fe(II)8L6 cubes use face-capping tetratopic porphyrin ligands (Mosquera et al., Nat Commun 2017, 8, 14882, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5379102)
column6: with the same ligands -> "with chelating (bis-bidentate) ligands in place of monodentate pyridyl linkers"; "(e.g., M₈L₆ cubes or M₄L₆ tetrahedra)" -> "(e.g., M₄L₆ tetrahedra, or M₈L₆ cubes with face-capping ligands)"
